title: Manager at Dell Sees AVC as a Key Thermal-Solution Partner as Second Sources Gain Share in AI Servers
expert: Development manager at Dell overseeing thermal supplier qualification and production quality
verdict: AVC supplies more than 70% of Dell's thermal solution and its scope grew 20% in the past year, but Dell expects second sources to reach 40%–50% of allocation on lead-time concerns.

Nvidia content and share: 🟢 More than 70% of Dell's thermal solution from AVC (first-hand), above JPM's ~50% AVC share per AI project (SB #58861). → Tenet 1 (Nvidia content and share) ↑

🔴 Second sources expected at 40%–50% of allocation (estimate), starting at 20%–30% after a 100-PO pilot, vs JPM's view that a 2–3 supplier preference limits share shift (SB #58861): conflicting. → Tenet 1 (Nvidia content and share) ↓
🟢 AVC thermal scope at Dell +20% in the past year (first-hand) vs AVC 3Q26 revenue +52% y/y (SB #63806): Dell growing slower than AVC overall.
Gross margin: 🟢 10%–20% premium for high-quality liquid cooling; liquid lifts total solution cost 20%–30%, 10%–20% from raw materials, consistent with AVC's cold-plate ASP raises (SB #58857). → Tenet 3 (GM 34%+) ↑
Rubin yield and ramp: 🟡 First-pass cold-plate yield must exceed 95% in mass production vs AVC VR200 yield ~60% in May (SB #64479): the bar AVC must clear.
🟢 Dell liquid-cooling business +70% next year (estimate), first read on Dell liquid growth.

changes: AVC >70% of Dell's thermal solution vs JPM's ~50% AVC share per AI project (SB #58861, 2026-09-29): higher at this OEM.
Second-source allocation expected at 40%–50% vs JPM's view that 2–3 supplier preference limits share shift (SB #58861): conflicting.
AVC thermal scope at Dell +20% y/y vs AVC company revenue +52% y/y in 3Q26 (SB #63806): slower at Dell.
Required first-pass yield >95% vs AVC VR200 yield ~60% in May (SB #64479): gap still to close.
thesis_impact: Tenet 1 (Nvidia content and share): ↓ — >70% share today but Dell plans second sources at 40%–50% of allocation.
Tenet 3 (Margin and EPS): ↑ — Dell would pay a 10%–20% premium for quality; liquid adds 20%–30% to solution cost.
Tenet 4 (Capacity and execution): ↓ — lead time is the stated reason for second-sourcing; mass production needs >95% first-pass yield.
